S-PECIFICATION FOR RATCHET LEVER HOIST

Prescribes materials, dimensions, general requirements and testing of ratchet lever hoist 1. Scopefitted with either link chain or roller chain -with lifting capacities of 0.8, 1'6, 3.2 and 5 tonnes.

2.0 For the purpose of this standard following

definitions

shall apply. by a lever through

2.1 Ratchet Lever Hoist - A portable tool fitted with a load chain and operated ratchet mechenism so as to give a mechanical advantage. 2.2 Working Load Limit The maximum mass which

a ratchet lever hoist can lift in general service. stated

2.3 Safe Working Load-The maximum mass which a ratchet lever hoist can lift in a particular service, It shall never be greater than the working load limit. 2.4 Rating or Capacity The safe working load in tonnes specified by the manufacturer

of the hoist.

2.5 Factor of Safety -- The ratio between the ultimate strength of the hoist as a unit and the rated load where the ultimate strength of the ratchet lever hoist is the maximum load on the load hook under which the load chain or any other component of the hoist gives way. 2.6 Efort - Average operating limit together with the effective 2.7 Range of-Lifting effort applied on the lever to raise a load equal to the working radius of the handle of the hoist. between the upper and lower limits of travel of the load hook. hook bed. the saddle of the load hook and load

4.4.1 Pawls shall be of sufficient strength to arrest the full ~load from lowering due to gravity. 4.4.2 The pawls shall engage with the ratchet wheel either by means of a spring other than-tension spring or by some other equally effective means. 4.4.3 It shall be so positioned mech,anism fail. that it engages the ratchet wheel under gravity, should its operating

4.4.4 Adequate arrangement shall be made to ensure that the pawl does not seize on the pawl pin. 4.4.5 The paw1 and the ratchet shall be made of steel duly heat treated to provide satisfactory The hardness of the pawl tip shall not be less degree of wear resistance together with toughness. than 40 HRC and that of ratchet not less than 30 HRC. 4.5 Suspension and bottom hook shall conform to IS: 3815-1969 Specification for point hooks 4.5.1 Hooks -Top with shank for general engineering purposes' or IS : 8610-1977 `Specification for point hooks with shank capacity up to 25 tonnes-trapezoidal section'. The bottom hooks shall be so designed that it shall be free to swivel in the loaded conditions without twisting the load chain. The top hook, if required to swivel, shall be fitted with plain bearings. Ball and roller bearing shall not be used. The continuous length of the shank engaged by nut on the load side shall at least be equal to 2/3 times the diameter of the shank before being interrupted by the drilling for split pins or other fixings unless the shank is shaped from the solid to afford the same degree of security as though fitted with-a nut. 4.5.2 Both the hooks shall be fitted uith safety catches. 4.5.3 Other fiffings sufficient strength. 4.5.4 All suspension shanks. 4.6 Load Chain 4.6.1 The load chain shall be of suitable grade and comply with the requirements standard, A terminal chain stop shall be provided at the free end of the chain. 4.6.1.1 Roller chain - Load chain of roller type shall conform to IS : 2403-1975 transmission steel roller chain and chain wheels ( first revision )`. of relevant ( fop and boffom blocks ) Suspension fittings other than hooks shall be of

4.6.1.2 Link chain - Calibrated short link alloy steel chain of minimum Grade 40 shall be used. It shall conform to IS : 3109 ( Part 2)-1982 `Specificatron for calibrated load chain for pulley blocks and other lifting appliances 1. ( second revision )`.
Note - Grade 80 chains conforming to IS : 6216-1982 `Short and other lifting appliances (first revision)' should be preferred link chain, grade T(8) calibrated as they have longer service life. for pulley blocks

4.6.2 Length of the chain -The total length of the load chain shall exceed the minimum length required to give the presented range of lift by not less than three links per fall to ensure that the slack end anchorage is not loaded. 4.6.3 Load chain wheel 4.6.3.1 For roller to IS : 2403-1975. chain It shall be made of suitable material duly heat treated and shall conform

4.6.3.2 For /ink chain - The load chain wheel shall be made of material suitable for use with load chain employed and be of adequate strength and shall be suitably designed to ensure effective operation of the chain. It shall be suitably heat treated for longer use. 4.6.4 Guidewheel. Means shall be provided to ensure effective guidance of the load chain into chain

8. Rating - Ratchet lever hoist shall be rated according to the safe working load, which in case of a hoist with multifalls shall be determined from the safe working load of the load chain, considering the angles introduced into the chain run and the friction occured during movement. These can be manufactured in the range of capacity 0'8, 1-6, 3.2 and 5.0 tonnes. effort on the lever required to raise a load radius of the operating lever of the hoist,

shall declare the operating 9. Effort - The manufacturer equal to the working load limit, together with the effective 10. Tests

10.1 Design 7'est -At the purchaser's option and expense a sample chain lever hoist or hoists shall be selected by the representative of the purchaser and shall be subjected to at least 4 times the working load limit for at least one minute, without breakage of material, partial or complete, or such distortion as could result in the release of the load. Following this test all parts shall be defaced to make them unusable. 10.2 OperationalProof Test - Each ratchet lever hoist shall be subjected by the manufacturer to an operational proof load of 1.5 times the safe working load through a lift which will ensure that each part of the hoist mechanism and each tooth of gear comes under load. examined by a competent 10.3 Examinafion - After the proof loading the hoist shall be thoroughly person. It complies with this standard only if it is found free from deformation, cracks, flaws and other defects. 4

IS'f 11340- 1985

APPENDIX ( Clause
RECOMkENDATlONS FOR USE AND 4.12 )

B

MAINTENANCE

OF

RATCHET

LEVER care.

HOISTS They should

B-l. Ratchet lever hoists are precision not be dropped from a height.

made and shouldbe

treated with appropriate

B-2. The ratchet lever hoist should never be subjected to greater load than the safe working load marked on the hoist. The hoist has been tested to more than this load, but it has been done under carefully controlled conditions. The use of a ratchet lever hoist at any load greater than the safe working load may result in damage. B-3. Attention is particularly Joad over uneven ground. B-4. drawn to the possibility of overloading a ratchet lever hoist when pulling

'

Never increase the length of the lever.

B-6. The chains should be well lubricated along their whole length and especially at the contact points between the links. Where oils and lubricants are not desirable, use a dry lubricant. Failure to maintain correct lubrication reduces the life of the chain. B-6. If the chain jumps should be replaced. or does not work smoothly or marks in use, it is probably out of pitch and

5

IS : 11340 - 1985
B-7. Before use, the chain should be examined to ensure that there is no twist. In the case of hoisting of chain, twist can arise from the chain hook being accidently turned over. Never load the point of the hook.
B-8. Never use a load chain or join it by bolts. as a sling, that is, by back hooking. Do not tie knots in the load chain

B-8. Do not allow dirt or hard grease to gather in the pockets of the sprokets. B-10. Never run the chain out too far. When the maximum range of travel is exceeded, an excessive and dangerous load is imposed on the load chain terminal stop.

B-11. It-should be made sure that the brake setting manufacturing instructions.

or adjustment

is maintained

in accordance with the
